course_title: Topics in Lit. & Environment: Planetary Futures
subject: ENG
course_description: A study of literary works of various genres and other imaginative writing about the relation of humans to the non-human world. Approaches may focus on particular genres, periods, or themes (e.g., ecofiction, ecopoetry, literature of climate change, multispecies writing, animal ethics, etc.).
course_notes: (Same as ENVS 385W 1) Topic: Planetary Futures How do writers represent our planet's present climate collapse and possible futures? In what ways does science fiction address ecological and sociopolitical questions? The primary work of this course will be reading, discussing, and writing about novels, supplemented by other media such as science journalism, poetry, and film. We will wrestle with the challenges of imagining both the slow violence of environmental catastrophe and alternatives to it. Writers may include Ursula K. Le Guin, Octavia E. Butler, and Kim Stanley Robinson, among others.
